small_guidance: The conv_transpose3d kernel itself looks correct (heavy op runs in Triton, max diff ~3e-3 suggests a BN folding issue, not a conv bug). Fix the BN fold: the reference uses BatchNorm3d in training mode (the harness never calls .eval()), so running_mean/var are NOT used — instead BN computes batch statistics. Replace the eval-style fold with training-mode stats: compute mean and var of y over dims=(0,2,3,4), then scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), shift=beta-mean*scale, and apply (y*scale+shift) before subtracting the per-(N,C) spatial mean. Also update batch_norm.running_mean/var with momentum to match nn.BatchNorm3d semantics if needed for subsequent calls.
large_guidance: Rewrite forward to faithfully model BatchNorm3d in training mode: (1) run the Triton conv_transpose3d to produce y; (2) launch a two-pass reduction kernel that computes per-channel mean_c and var_c over (N,D,H,W); (3) launch a fused epilogue kernel that, per (n,c) row, first computes the per-(n,c) spatial mean of the BN-normalized values, then writes out gamma*(y-mean_c)/sqrt(var_c+eps)+beta - spatial_mean. Keep the conv kernel as-is (it appears correct). Consider channels_last layout for the conv output to make the BN per-channel reduction coalesced.
